bull_bear.body:
- The deck discloses no dividend, buyback or capital-allocation policy, and no leverage or return target.
- Audited consolidated balance sheet as presented (March-26 vs March-25, Rs Crs): Total Equity 319 vs 293; non-current Borrowings 55 vs 35; current Borrowings 301 vs 234; Inventories 300 vs 213; Trade Receivable 59 vs 69; Total Assets 740 vs 624.
- FY26 audited cash flow as presented (Rs Crs): Net Cash from Operating Activities 0.91; Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities -60.05; Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities 59.78; Changes in Working Capital -85.85.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- The deck splits the business into three segments: 'B2B - Terpene' (Camphor, Dipentene, Sodium Acetate, Isobornyl Acetate, Isoborneol), 'B2B - Synthetic Resin' (Terpene Phenolic Resin, Alkyl Phenolic Resin, Rosin Ester) and 'B2C - Retail Operations' (CamPure, 'Mangalam' camphor tablets, private labelling initiatives).
- End-markets are named per terpene product: camphor into 'Religious use, healthcare products, hygiene products'; dipentene into 'Paints, cleaning and degreasing agents'; sodium acetate into 'Textile and dyes industry, Leather tanning'; isobornyl acetate and isoborneol into 'Fragrance and flavor'.
- Resin end-markets are named as adhesives (Terpene Phenolic Resin), 'Rubber Products i.e. Tyers' (Alkyl Phenolic Resin) and, for Rosin Ester, 'Paint and varnish material industry, thermoplastic compounds for road marking, hot melts and glues susceptible to pressure, insulation finishes'.
- CamPure is positioned as extending camphor 'beyond traditional use and into homes, wardrobes, cars, bathrooms and Personal Spaces', with cones, Insta pouches, surface cleaners, automatic fresheners and car fragrance solutions.
- The sales-network slide claims 'PAN India Presence With Growing Export Footprints', mapping a manufacturing plant, head office, a warehouse & marketing office and marketing offices; the deck flags the map as 'not to scale. For illustrative purpose only.'
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group entity] The deck carries a standalone results table for 'Mangalam Brands Private limited' but never states the entity's relationship to Mangalam Organics - no ownership stake, no role, and no statement of whether it is inside the consolidated numbers shown elsewhere in the deck.
- [Leadership] Promoter-family led: Chairman Mr. Kamalkumar Dujodwala (42+ years in the chemical industry, Chairman since 2007) and Managing Director Mr. Pannkaj Dujodwala (35+ years 'in the Pine Chemicals Industry'); Chief Strategy Officer Mr. Akshay Dujodwala heads Retail Sales and Marketing and is described as 'instrumental in transforming the company from a B2B to B2C player'.
- [Leadership tenure] CEO Mr. Sanjay Bhardwaj, a Chartered Accountant, is stated to have been with the company 'for the past 30 years, starting from November 1, 1994'; CFO Mr. Manoj Mhapadi is a CA with 20 years' experience; Company Secretary Ms. Charmi Shah has 'Over three years of experience' in the secretarial and compliance field.
- [Board bio anomaly] The independent-director entry for Mr. Sudarshan Kumar Saraf describes him as 'Co-Chairman and Managing Director aged 60+' and lists directorships at BMS Industries, Ashrit Holdings, Technosoft Engineering Projects, Anhui Reliable Steel Technology (China), Technocraft International (UK) and Technocraft Trading Spolka, without naming the company at which he holds that Co-Chairman/Managing Director role.

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Mangalam Organics as a single-plant camphor and terpene chemicals manufacturer at Kumbhivali (Khalapur, Raigad) selling B2B terpenes and synthetic resins, now pushing into a B2C camphor-based consumer brand, 'CamPure', through e-commerce and an expanding salesforce.
